assumptions: Quenched nearest-neighbor kernel uniformly bounded below by kappa>0

statement: For a kappa-uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor chain, successive exits from sets selected at finite stopping times and fixed during each residence, with deterministic escape radius <=r, define sigma_m and K_tau=min{m>=1:sigma_m>=tau}. For any positive integer random horizon tau finite on B, P(B)=p>0, E[tau|B]<infinity iff E[K_tau|B]<infinity; E[K_tau|B]<=E[tau|B]<=ceil(8r*log(4/3)/kappa^r)*(E[K_tau|B]+3/p). tau and B may depend on the future.
assumptions: Each set is selected at sigma_i and stays fixed until exit
tau>=1 integer valued and finite on event B
proof_or_counterexample: LEMMA_CLOCK_TO_COUNT.md: conditional exponential moment <=4/3 at lambda=kappa^r/(4r); tower property for sigma_m; unconditional Chernoff followed by division by p once; tail summation. No optional stopping at tau.

remaining_gap: To prove C0041 by this route, establish finite conditional mean K_tau for the directional regeneration horizon from directional transience and spatial iid.

statement: For every fixed 0<kappa<1/4, homogeneous iid environments on Z^2 with row (1/4+delta,1/4-delta,1/4,1/4), 0<delta<=1/4-kappa, are kappa-uniformly elliptic and ballistic in e1, but their expected total occupation of {0} is unbounded across delta, while first singleton exit time is identically 1. For each individual delta>0 total occupation has finite expectation.
assumptions: Same fixed ellipticity lower bound kappa<1/4
Degenerate iid environment law at the displayed row
proof_or_counterexample: LEMMA_RETURN_OBSTRUCTION.md: iid increment strong law, central-binomial return lower bound, finite-time path comparison giving G_delta>=1+(1/8)H_N for delta<=1/(16N), and an exponential tilt giving finiteness for each delta.

remaining_gap: This refutes a law-independent occupation shortcut only; it does not refute C0041 or fixed-law regeneration integrability.
